must_catch.item: The real trigger is the CFO's month-end close, not the portal.
No dollar figure is stated. The rep doesn't know it.
The global/infrastructure opener is reported as silence.

data.notes: The report gets the core story right. The portal was the way in, but the real trigger was the CFO's month-end close, and the deal turned on a value case built from her own data ('that's my number, not yours'). It keeps Fiserv's pitch unknown and only relays the rep's vague 'low six figures' recollection while flagging the exact figure as a follow-up with Wen. Its main miss is the competitor insight: it never reads the named-contact request (her bank rep had changed) as a sign the bank relationship was weaker than it looked, and it hedges on the rate-versus-problem mismatch. It also invents a few non-existent 'inconsistencies': an off-the-shelf portal versus 'building', and three weeks versus a month. Finally, it labels an answered question as dodged.
